stem: On August 29, 1947, the Drafting Committee of the Constitution was formed, with Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as its Chairman and six other members. Who among the following was not a member of this committee?
expl: To consider the draft of the Constitution prepared by the Constitutional Adviser of the Constituent Assembly, B.N. Rau, the Drafting Committee was constituted on 29 August, 1947, under the chairmanship of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. Its six other members were—Gopalaswami Ayyangar, Kanhaiyalal Maneklal Munshi, Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar, Syed Muhammad Saadullah, B.L. Mitra, and D.P. Khaitan. Later, N. Madhava Rao was included in place of B.L. Mitra, and after the death of D.P. Khaitan in 1948, T.T. Krishnamachari was included in the committee. Jawaharlal Nehru was not a member of this committee.

stem: Who among the following was the first chairman of the Business Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
expl: The first Chairman of the Constituent Assembly’s Order of Business Committee was Kanhaiyalal Maneklal Munshi. He was elected to the Constituent Assembly from Bombay (Mumbai) on the Congress party ticket. Therefore, in the given question, the mention of “Business committee” is incorrect.

stem: The phrase 'equality before law' used in Article 14 of the Indian Constitution has been borrowed from the Constitution of

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Article 14 of the Indian Constitution states that the State (India) shall not deny to any person within its territory equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws. A special feature of this provision is that it applies equally to citizens as well as foreigners. Here, “equality before law” is taken from the British tradition (since Britain/Great Britain does not have a written constitution). The concept of “equal protection of the laws” has been taken from the American Constitution.

stem: Where did the inspiration for 'liberty, Equality and Fraternity' come from?
expl: The French Revolution of 1789 was a reaction against an absolute monarchy. The slogan of this revolution was “Liberty, Equality and Fraternity”. This idea came from the inspiration of the French Revolution.
